status: Research only; no canon or released files changed
primary_access_limit: No complete primary fiction edition independently read. Evidence combines quoted fictional passages within accessible scholarship, detailed critical reconstructions, and primary author testimony.
method: HTTP fetch through configured network; SHA-256 of raw response bytes; HTML tags stripped or pdftotext -layout streamed in memory. Pérez scanned PDF additionally rendered and OCRed in memory. No full contemporary source body or PDF retained.
quote_policy: Each source retains at most80 words of locator excerpts here; dossier primarily paraphrases. Locator line breaks normalized. Source titles are bibliographic labels.

sources.author: Ethan Weed
sources.title: A Labyrinth of Symbols: Exploring “The Garden of Forking Paths”
sources.evidence_grade: B: journal close reading; embedded quotations are narrower primary evidence
sources.inspected_scope: Printed pp.163–168 and 172–179 displayed and inspected; intervening material and later pages were not fully read.
sources.supports: Layered framing, delayed murder motive, interpretation of the inset book, differences between inset temporal model and enclosing events.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: But it doesn’t seem that “The Garden” has the same sort of internal inconsistencies as in Ts’ui Pên’s novel
But in the story, the parallel universes are universes in which the events stay the same, and the only thing that alters is the way they are perceived.

sources.limitations: Weed’s causal-timing objection about the newspapers and his reading of Albert’s attitude to death remain interpretations, not established alternate solutions.

sources.author: Iván Almeida
sources.title: La circularidad de las ruinas: Variaciones de Borges sobre un tema cartesiano
sources.evidence_grade: B: journal philosophical reading with quoted primary passages
sources.inspected_scope: Opening and selected keyword contexts; printed pp.69–73 read continuously; relevant portions of pp.84–86 inspected.
sources.supports: Creator/creation reversal, dream construction methods, Fire’s layered representation, and distinction between plot and critic’s immanence interpretation.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: no se trata de saber si la creatura está o no soñando, sino si está o no siendo soñada.
“Fuego” es, no su realidad, sino únicamente su “nombre terrenal”.

sources.limitations: Almeida’s final “natura sine Deo” interpretation and his inference that only creators are dreamed are not adopted as facts established by the story. Locators normalize PDF line breaks.

sources.author: Genaro J. Pérez
sources.title: The Circular Ruins
sources.publication: Reference Guide to Short Fiction, ed. Noelle Watson, St. James Press, 1994, pp.669–670; bibliography verified against Borges Center catalog
sources.evidence_grade: B: specialist reference entry providing detailed plot synopsis
sources.inspected_scope: PDF cover and complete entry on printed pp.669–670 inspected through in-memory OCR of all three scanned PDF pages; unrelated neighboring entries not used.
sources.supports: Failed selection, construction from a heart, erased apprenticeship, report of son’s immunity, maker’s own immunity and recognition.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: the gray man had been haunted by the impression that all this had already happened.
he discovered to his humiliation that the fire did not affect his flesh

sources.limitations: PDF has no usable text layer. Quoted locators are short OCR transcriptions, not a claim of diplomatic transcription. The entry’s causal, concentric, theological and literary analogies remain critical interpretations.

sources.author: John Clute [JC]
sources.title: Wolfe, Gene
sources.publication: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction, online entry
sources.inspected_scope: Paragraph on The Fifth Head of Cerberus, publication bibliography entry, and author signature inspected; unrelated novel material not used.
sources.supports: Three interdependent narratives, identity/anthropology/cloning, and inference through rereading.

locator_excerpts.locator: Paragraph beginning “His next, The Fifth Head of Cerberus”
locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: all so closely linked as to be significantly less effective in isolation
the book as a whole could technically be described as a collection of linked stories; but that would be misleadingly simple.

sources.limitations: Used to establish the formal interdependence and publication, not to import other Wolfe cosmologies.

sources.author: Peter Wright
sources.title: Confounding the Skin and the Mask: Gene Wolfe’s The Fifth Head of Cerberus and the Politics of Ambiguity
sources.publication: Paper presented at Gene Wolfe conference, University of Birmingham, 26 August 2000; author-permitted republication on Ultan’s Library
sources.evidence_grade: B: scholarly conference paper; political and ethical conclusions are interpretations
sources.inspected_scope: Opening argument read continuously through the discussion of Marsch/Trenchard hybridity; later identity/authorship and prison conclusion passages inspected in keyword contexts; notes inspected.
sources.supports: Replication across generations, Veil’s hypothesis, researcher/subject reversal, disputed authorship of the middle tale, colonial classification.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: Who produces this text? Is it Marsch or Marsch-Trenchard?
If it is Marsch, then it becomes another piece of colonial fakery, the white interpretation of a barely comprehended alien culture.

sources.limitations: Wright’s favorable account of the hybrid is disputed by Borski. “One and the same person” across clones is treated as Wright’s compression, not a settled equation of genome and personhood. Site explicitly states author permission.

sources.author: Robert Borski
sources.title: The Fifth Head of Cerberus reviewed
sources.inspected_scope: Complete substantive review body read across initial output and follow-up character slices; navigation/comments excluded.
sources.supports: First narrative’s family and experimental context; middle story’s attribution; documents and chronology in V.R.T.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: Characters met in the first novella reappear in the third
Little is told chronologically, and often mundanities from the present-time narrative intrude

sources.limitations: Claims about decoded names, every identity, and unnamed officer are not adopted. Concrete narrative framing is used alongside Wright and Wolfe testimony.

sources.author: Robert Borski
sources.title: Desanctifying Victor Trenchard: some notes on Peter Wright’s “Confounding the Skin and the Mask”
sources.publication: Written December 2001; posted 24 May 2002, Ultan’s Library
sources.evidence_grade: B: specialist critical response; individual speculative identifications remain C
sources.inspected_scope: Complete substantive response, numbered parallels, and footnotes read; navigation excluded.
sources.supports: Explicit dispute with Wright’s favorable ethical interpretation; repeated parallels between Number Five and Victor.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: Number Five are symbolic twins, with life circumstances and ultimate fates irrevocably linked
another attempt at relaxation–part of a successive set of interpretations.

sources.limitations: Borski’s violent-act attribution, mother identification, name decipherments and speculative footnotes are not silently promoted to neutral plot facts. The dossier reports his ethical challenge as a challenge.

sources.author: Larry McCaffery interviewing Gene Wolfe
sources.title: On Encompassing the Entire Universe: An Interview with Gene Wolfe
sources.publication: Science Fiction Studies 46, vol.15 part3, November1988; accessed through Gwern HTML mirror
sources.evidence_grade: A for Wolfe’s stated narrative design/intention, with mirror-provenance qualification
sources.inspected_scope: Cerberus ordering exchange and complete ensuing identity/marksmanship answer inspected; surrounding background, revision and memory excerpts inspected selectively.
sources.supports: Why the researcher precedes the legend; preservation of narrative present; intention that the guide’s replacement of Marsch be inferable.

locator_excerpts.locator: Answer beginning “No, because I didn’t want to show”
locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: I decided to present the Sandwalker story as a legend or story that Marsch had uncovered, rather than as straight reportage

locator_excerpts.locator: Answer beginning “In the end, of course”
locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: both V.R.T. and the narrator are shown to be very poor shots, whereas Marsch is a very good shot

locator_excerpts.locator: Same answer, following the guide/shapeshifter sentence

sources.limitations: Original journal issue not retrieved. Mirror includes inconsistent added year metadata; journal citation is November1988. Authorial explanation strongly supports the guide substitution, without settling every symbolic or moral interpretation.

sources.author: Marc Aramini
sources.title: Proving Veil’s Hypothesis: Variance Reduction Techniques, Larval Life Cycles on an East Wind, and Shadow Children Riding Mars(c)hmen in The Fifth Head of Cerberus
sources.evidence_grade: C: explicit competing total reconstruction grounded in selected passages
sources.inspected_scope: Opening claim, methodological premise, and targeted Shadow Children/cat/tools/Christian-symbolism passages inspected; complete article not read.
sources.supports: Documents an alternative parasitic-identity reconstruction and the need to distinguish inferred total models from author-confirmed local events.

locator_excerpts.exact_excerpt: the journals in “V.R.T.” are authored by a parasitic Shadow Child who has taken Marsch’s place instead of by Victor R. Trenchard.

sources.limitations: Not adopted as established fictional ontology. Claimed early/later edition pronoun differences were encountered but editions were not inspected and that textual claim is not used. Christian allusions do not establish a literally intervening deity.
